exceptions.title: Admission pulse: 90 or 80
exceptions.body: The nurse's record at 7 pm on 5 Nov reads PR 90 bpm, written over an earlier figure, and the handover sheet also says 90. The nursing initial assessment form of the same evening says 80 b/mt. 90 is shown until you decide.

exceptions.title: Catheter insertion date: 5 Nov or 6 Nov
exceptions.body: The insertion bundle and the nursing initial assessment say the urinary catheter was inserted on 5/11/26 (5:40 PM). The maintenance bundle writes the date of insertion as 6/11/26. 5 Nov is shown.

exceptions.title: CT pulmonary angiogram page is headed 6/11/26
exceptions.body: The sheet with the CT entries (8:45 am received at CT, 9:05 done) is headed 6/11/26 - continue. The nurse's record of 7/11 sends the patient to CT for CTPA at 8:30 am and the next page, headed 7/11/26, receives the patient back at 9:45 am. The CT is dated 7 Nov here.

exceptions.title: Blood pressure on the morning of discharge
exceptions.body: The MEWS chart for 12 Nov marks systolic at 130 with diastolic written as 80. The blood pressure chart arrow for 8 AM on 12/11/26 reads about 120-130 over about 70. Both are read off hand-drawn charts.

exceptions.title: Two GRBS values on 8 Nov can be read two ways
exceptions.body: On the insulin chart the 10:30 am value is read as 293 (could be 223) and the 3 pm value as 298 (could be 228). The time of the 250 reading is unclear on the chart; the nurse's record gives it at about 8 pm. The first row of the second insulin chart page has an overwritten date (10 or 11/11/26); it matches the nurse's record of 11 Nov.

exceptions.title: One nurse's entries on 9 to 12 Nov are only partly readable
exceptions.body: The entries on drain removal, dressing change, physiotherapy and catheter removal are in hard handwriting. Catheter removal at 9:30 pm on 10 Nov is confirmed by the maintenance bundle. Drain removal and physiotherapy on 9 Nov rest on this reading alone.

exceptions.title: Antibiotics were sent to theatre; giving is not recorded here
exceptions.body: Advent 1.2 g, Ticocin 400 mg and Vancomycin 1 g (2 vials) are listed as sent to the operating theatre with the patient on 7 Nov. This PDF does not say when or whether each was given. One name is spelt two ways on the two pages and is read as Ticocin.

exceptions.title: IV entries on the intake charts of 10 to 12 Nov
exceptions.body: The IV column on these charts is hard to read. The 1 pm entry on 11 Nov is read as Inj. Tramadol 50 mg added in 100 ml NS. The night entries on 10 and 11 Nov and the 7 am entries on 11 and 12 Nov (100 ml each) could not be named with confidence.

exceptions.title: Year of the past skin surgery is hidden
exceptions.body: The nutritional assessment writes SCC of the right gluteal skin, s/p wide excision, with a year in brackets that is partly covered by a number stamp. It is read as 2017 with doubt.

timeline.title: Admitted
timeline.detail: Orthopaedics. Left femur neck fracture. On 4 L oxygen, with Foley catheter and skin traction on the left leg.

timeline.title: Work-up before surgery
timeline.detail: Medicine and pulmonary consultations, serology, 2 units PRBC cross-matched, PAC chart viewed.

timeline.title: CT pulmonary angiogram
timeline.detail: Done in the morning before surgery. Report not in this PDF.

timeline.title: Surgery
timeline.detail: Left bipolar hemiarthroplasty under spinal anaesthesia. Drain in the left hip. To HDU at 5 pm.

timeline.title: Day 1 after surgery
timeline.detail: GRBS 263, Actrapid started and Glimy M1 withheld. Clexane 0.4 ml. Shifted from HDU to the ward on 1 L oxygen.

timeline.title: Oxygen trial off
timeline.detail: Oxygen stopped in the morning. SpO2 89% on room air at 4:20 pm, restarted at 1 L.

timeline.title: Catheter removed
timeline.detail: Urinary catheter removed at 9:30 pm. Knee immobilizer advised. NT-pro BNP sent.

timeline.title: Discharged
timeline.detail: General condition good, vitals stable. All lines and catheter removed.

notes: This PDF is the nursing half of one admission (5 to 12 Nov 2026): the discharge summary, doctors' notes, drug chart, operative and anaesthesia records and all lab and imaging reports are expected in another PDF of the same folder, so the diagnosis here is kept as working (provisional on the plan of care) and should give way to the discharge summary. The same diagnosis, allergy statement and vitals repeat on the handover sheets (pages 114 to 121), care plans (98 to 113) and charts (128 to 139); they are cited once with a few also-citations. How the patient came in is not stated: the first cannula is marked as inserted by 'yellow area' at 1:35 pm and the catheter location as 'RTR YA' at 5:40 pm on 5 Nov, before the ward arrival at 7 pm, which may mean the emergency area, so entry is left null. PTCD / PTCT is written for the pulmonary team that was consulted; the expansion is not written in the file. Nurse's record sheets are slightly out of time order around the CT (page 62 is headed 6/11 but belongs to the morning of 7 Nov). A medico-legal case was noted as not required (page 61). GRBS has no printed range, so no value is flagged high or low. Antibiotic names are as the nurses wrote them (Advent, Ticocin, Vancomycin); the nurses' record does not give times of administration. Staff names appear on many pages and are left out. The I.P. number in encounters[].ref is read from the handwritten admission order.
